source_of_truth: this file; the Nomad backend's contract test fails when the code and this file disagree
description: How an Aseman workload (A501/A503) becomes a Nomad job, and how Nomad's allocation state becomes an Aseman observation. Nomad servers are the VMM control plane; Nomad clients are workers. Nothing here changes the node-facing A501 contract.

job.comment: One workload is one job with one group and one task. The workload UUID is the job ID, so registration is idempotent and a workload can never place twice.

meta.aseman.owner: the node identity that owns the workload (A501 owner)
meta.aseman.generation: the desired generation this job spec was written for

job.comment_generation: The observation's generation is read back from the job's meta, never from the request, so a stale allocation is never reported as the current generation.

actions.start: register the job at the desired generation with count 1; the register is a plain PUT, so repeating it is harmless
actions.stop: register the same job with count 0; the allocations stop and the job stays, so a restart keeps the workload's identity
actions.delete: stop the job with purge=true; a purge of an unknown job is success
actions.pause: refused: Nomad has no allocation-level pause. A runtime that pauses does it through the worker agent (ADR 0010), never by stopping the group

resources.cpu_mhz: resources.vcpu_millis, floored to Nomad's minimum of 1 MHz per the rule below
resources.cpu_rule: vcpu_millis is thousandths of a core; Nomad wants MHz. One core is declared as 1000 MHz, so cpu_mhz = max(1, vcpu_millis)
resources.disk_mb: resources.disk_mib when set, else the group default of 300

network.mode: the operator's CNI network (`cni/{name}`), or Nomad's plain `bridge`
network.comment: A workload gets its own network namespace. Host mode is never used: it would put the workload on the host's network with no policy.
network.ingress: each spec.network.ingress port becomes a group port with the same label; an http port is also registered as a service for discovery
network.egress_deny_by_default: an empty `egress_allow` means the workload reaches nothing. Nomad's plain bridge cannot deliver that, so a deny-by-default workload is refused there; the operator supplies a CNI network that enforces it and declares that it does
network.egress_allow_entries: refused: nothing in this mapping can express a per-destination allowance, so it is never widened to everything nor narrowed to nothing
network.guest_api: spec.bootstrap.guest_api_url is passed to the task as ASEMAN_GUEST_API; the address must be reachable from the allocation's namespace

docker.comment: The Nomad Docker driver, not the Aseman docker plugin: Nomad owns the container's life.

qemu.comment: Used only when the artifact is a bootable image the QEMU driver accepts.

javascript.image: the runner image for the runtime

wasm.image: the runner image for the runtime

elpian.image: the runner image for the runtime

elpify.image: the runner image for the runtime

firecracker.comment: Nomad schedules an unprivileged runner task; the microVM itself is the worker agent's (ADR 0010). P6-05.

forbidden.raw_exec: raw_exec does not isolate a workload and is never used, in any mode
forbidden.exec_privileged: the docker driver's privileged mode, host network, host PID, and host bind mounts are never set by the mapping

runner.comment: A runtime with no image of its own runs in a hardened OCI runner task that fetches the program artifact with the workload credential and executes it. The runner image is declared per runtime by the operator; the mapping never invents one.
runner.credential: the workload credential is written to the task's secrets directory as bootstrap.credential and never appears in meta, env, or the job spec Nomad stores in plain text

observation.comment: The observed state is read from the workload's allocations, newest first. A job with no allocation is Pending while its evaluation is open and Stopped once it is not.
observation.reason: the allocation's task event message, when it has one; never the raw Nomad struct

data_plane.logs: GET /v1/client/allocation/{alloc}/logs for stdout and stderr; the record's sequence is the byte offset the reader continues from
data_plane.exec: POST /v1/client/allocation/{alloc}/exec (websocket), only for a runtime whose capabilities declare exec
data_plane.endpoints: the allocation's network addresses and their labelled ports
data_plane.forward_http: an HTTP request to the allocation's http port; the VMM never reaches a workload by any other address
data_plane.files: GET/POST /v1/client/fs on the allocation directory, only for a runtime whose capabilities declare files
data_plane.build: not the scheduler's: an image is built before registration and the job names the built reference

identity.comment: Nomad workload identity proves which allocation is calling. It never authorizes an Aseman operation on its own: the workload signs its guest-API calls with its Aseman credential (A405).
identity.acl: the backend's Nomad token is scoped to the aseman namespace and to job, alloc, and node read/write; it has no operator or ACL rights

federation.comment: The whole Nomad cluster is one Aseman node. Adding or removing a worker, or losing a server, never changes the Aseman node identity or its federation address.

capabilities.comment: The backend declares the runtime's capabilities with everything Nomad cannot deliver masked off. It never claims more than it can do.

masked_off.pause: Nomad has no allocation-level pause (P6-05, ADR 0010)
masked_off.exec: Nomad's exec is a websocket this backend does not speak yet (P6-05)
masked_off.build: an image is built before registration; the scheduler does not build
masked_off.files_write: Nomad's client API reads an allocation directory; it does not write one

narrowed.invocation: only for a runtime that also serves HTTP ingress: the ingress is the only way into an allocation the mapping gives
narrowed.execution_proofs: only under a runner image, which is what would carry them out
